_readme: THE DEFINITION-OF-DONE REGISTER — [pipeline N-1] company/pipeline/06-app-build.md
The machine-readable half of the factory's Definition of Done: one row per DoD item, each naming
HOW it is enforced. The prose one-pager lives at company/requirements/definition-of-done.md and
POINTS AT THIS FILE rather than restating it — the items live in one place, or they drift in two.
WHY THE SPLIT, AND WHY THIS HALF IS PUBLIC.
The stage doc's acceptance for N-1 asks CI to parse company/MASTER_PLAN.md §4 and the DoD page.
Both live under company/, which is GITIGNORED — CI cannot read either, so as written the
requirement was unenforceable from the only place a build can fail. Exactly the class of blocker
stage 8 hit, and its resolution there was to give the machine-checkable half an in-tree home
(tooling/legal/); this mirrors that reasoning. So:
· tooling/dod-register.json (HERE, public)      — what a guard can check, and does:
tooling/ci/assert-app-dod.mjs.
· company/requirements/definition-of-done.md    — the one-page prose version, private.
· tooling/scripts/check-dod-sync.mjs            — a LOCAL check, the only place with read
access to BOTH trees. It asserts this
register's item ids are set-equal to
MASTER_PLAN §4's lettered items and to the
prose page's, and that no dated cut has crept
back onto the page. What CI cannot see, it
PRINTS rather than silently omitting.
FIELDS.
id          the MASTER_PLAN §4 letter. The set of ids here must equal the set of letters there;
adding a letter to §4 without adding a row here fails check-dod-sync.mjs.
title       short name, for messages.
enforcedBy  'guard' | 'lane' | 'human'. There is no fourth value and no blank.
check       guard  -> the filename in tooling/ci/ that enforces it. assert-app-dod.mjs resolves
it to a `run:` step on a NON-COMMENT line, in a workflow whose `on:`
includes push, whose job is in ci-gate's `needs:`. Presence of the file is
NOT sufficient — a guard nothing runs cannot fail a build.
lane   -> the ci.yml job name. Same last clause: it must be in ci-gate's `needs:`.
human  -> the humanReview row id in every app's dod.json that carries the verdict.
humanHalf   optional. Names the humanReview row that carries the JUDGMENT half of an item whose
mechanical half is guarded. It must name a real required humanReview row, so an item
cannot point its human half at nothing.
why         the sentence that justifies the enforcement choice.
THE CUT LIST IS PART OF THE CONTRACT, NOT AN APPENDIX. Every entry is a DoD sub-item that was
deliberately priced out, with the date and the decision that cut it. check-dod-sync.mjs fails if a
cut phrase reappears in the prose page's ITEMS section — a cut that quietly returns is how a
one-pager becomes a four-pager again, which is what rotted the first time.
`reclaimed` — A THIRD LIST, ADDED 2026-08-13, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE A CUT IS NOT THE ONLY WAY OUT.
A criterion that the tree ALREADY SATISFIES belongs in neither list: cutting it publishes a false
admission, and requiring it invents debt that is already paid. Each row names the SC, its WCAG LEVEL,
the file:line that satisfies it TODAY, and the cheap guard that would keep it satisfied. The guards
are `⬜ NOT BUILT` and say so on every row — a named guard is not an enforced guard, and this register
is the last place that should blur the two.
🔴 WHY THE LEVEL FIELD IS NOT DECORATION. WCAG 2.2 §5.2.1: for Level AA conformance the page must
satisfy ALL Level A and Level AA success criteria. Two of the criteria cut on 2026-08-13 (SC 3.2.6
and SC 3.3.7) are LEVEL A. Cutting a Level A criterion while an app's store listing publishes
'Accessible — WCAG 2.2 AA' makes that claim false by construction, and MASTER_PLAN.md §4-F's
'Why a criterion in neither list is the bug' paragraph (:222 as measured 2026-08-13 — anchored by its
TEXT because the line moves, which it already did once today) routes that claim through [8]K-3: every
published legal claim is asserted true of the code. The level is what makes a cut checkable against
the claim instead of against taste.
`aaaAdopted` / `aaaNotAdopted` / `aaaAwaitingOwner` — A FOURTH, FIFTH AND SIXTH LIST, ADDED 2026-08-13.
The owner's decision that day: Level AA everywhere, PLUS a NAMED SET of AAA criteria that are free or
chassis-cheap. FULL AAA IS REJECTED, on W3C's own advice — WCAG 2.2 §5.2.1 Note 2, verbatim: "It is not
recommended that Level AAA conformance be required as a general policy for entire sites because it is
not possible to satisfy all Level AAA success criteria for some content."
🔴 WHY THREE LISTS AND NOT TWO, AND WHY THE THIRD IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. The whole §4-F thread exists
because SEVEN criteria sat in neither the required nor the cut list and nobody noticed. Applying that
same rule to the AAA set is what these lists are for: WCAG 2.2 has 31 AAA success criteria, and every
one of them is now in exactly one list. 20 adopted · 10 not adopted · 1 (SC 2.2.4 Interruptions) that
the owner's brief did not name at all, parked in `aaaAwaitingOwner` rather than silently sorted by an
agent. Filing an unnamed criterion into a list the owner never chose is the SAME defect as the
2026-08-13 over-cut, in the same direction: a classification nobody made, read later as one somebody did.
🔴 THE COUNT IN THE BRIEF WAS 18 AND THE ENUMERATION IS 20 — measured by listing them, 2026-08-13.
4 already-satisfied + 5 satisfied-by-absence + 10 chassis-build + 1 with-carve-out = 20. The brief's own
count contradicted its own list, which is the exact shape CLAUDE.md records for the 5-of-6/4-of-6
platform line. The enumeration governs; 20 is the number, and 20 + 10 + 1 = 31 closes the AAA set.
⚠️ THE CLAIM DOES NOT CHANGE, AND `claimWording` BELOW IS WHY. There is no "AA+" and no "partial AAA":
§5.2.1 is all-or-nothing per level. The published claim stays LEVEL AA, with this adopted list attached
as §5.3.2's OPTIONAL component. Never reach for §5.4 Statement of Partial Conformance — that clause is
for uncontrolled third-party content, and misusing it misstates a defined term of the standard.
⬜ ADOPTED IS NOT MET. Rows carry `state` and, where it is not met, `unmetDebt: true`. Contrast and
reduce-motion are MEASURED UNBUILT and stay ⬜ debt exactly as the 2026-08-13 adoption left them;
[2]C-14's rung is NOT raised by any row here. A guard named in `guard` with `guardStatus` ⬜ NOT BUILT
is a specification, never coverage — the same warning the `reclaimed` rows carry, for the same reason.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-app-dod.mjs (public half) + tooling/scripts/check-dod-sync.mjs (local).
NOTE: check-dod-sync.mjs does NOT read these three lists — it reads `items` and `cuts` only. That is
stated rather than discovered: these rows are prose on both sides today, exactly as `reclaimed` is.
source: company/MASTER_PLAN.md §4 — 'Per-app production checklist = reusable Definition of Done', items A-H

items.title: Complete screen set
items.why: the non-app-specific screens ship in the chassis, so the register of 22 screens plus its anchors is what makes 'complete' a query rather than a memory [C-13]

items.title: Four distinguishable states on every data screen
items.why: 39-CHASSIS §6 downgraded widget-per-state from CI: seven screens x fifty apps of golden-backed state widgets is unaffordable. The judgment stays; the RECORDING of it is mechanical [N-8]

items.title: Adaptive — five Material window classes
items.why: the 'ui-invariants-inherited' property pins the five classes at their exact Material edges; the tree once covered three and 600-639 got the phone layout

items.title: Dark mode, persisted
items.why: 'theme-triplet-supplied' plus 'theme-mode-persisted' anchor BOTH limbs — the write and the read-back — because a choice saved and never restored looks exactly like no persistence at all

items.title: Localized — zero hardcoded strings
items.why: l10n retrofitted across fifty shipped apps is the canonical near-free-at-birth item; the chassis also ships a second locale so the seam can actually be exercised

items.title: Accessible — the mechanical WCAG 2.2 limbs
items.why: text-scale clamp, 48px targets and non-empty icon labels are asserted on the stamped app; the manual screen-reader pass is a recorded cut (no Apple device) and stays a11y debt, not a gate. 48px is the HOUSE standard, NOT the WCAG figure — WCAG 2.2 AA's floor is SC 2.5.8 at 24x24 CSS px and 48 is Material's; relabelled in MASTER_PLAN 4-F on 2026-08-13 so nobody reads '48px, WCAG' and concludes something false. The number itself is unchanged here and in chassis_properties_test.dart (greaterThanOrEqualTo(48.0)), because loosening a shipped, negative-tested invariant to 24 buys nothing. WIDENED 2026-08-13: 4.5:1 contrast (SC 1.4.3, AA) was adopted into [2]C-14 as an OWED acceptance, together with reduce-motion (SC 2.3.3, which is LEVEL AAA and is therefore a HOUSE EXTRA, not part of the AA claim) — neither is built; disableAnimations and contrastRatio both measure 0 occurrences in source. ~~the other five WCAG criteria DoD 4-F named are the five cuts dated 2026-08-13 below~~ REVERSED SAME DAY, 2026-08-13, and the retraction is the point: FOUR of those five were measured SATISFIED by the tree that already ships (SC 2.5.7, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8 — see `reclaimed`), and two of them are LEVEL A, so cutting them contradicted the published 'WCAG 2.2 AA' claim under WCAG §5.2.1. One cut survives as a cut and it was narrowed: SC 2.4.11's CI GATE is cut, the CRITERION stays owed AA debt in [2]C-14

items.title: Polished — the app's own brand icon and splash
items.why: the mechanical half is that the stamp generates the app's OWN icons rather than shipping Flutter's stock ones — measured against the live SDK's assets, never pinned hashes. Motion tokens, skeletons-not-spinners and friendly empty/error states are judgment and live in the humanHalf row

items.title: Proven — the app analyzes clean and its own suite passes
items.why: the lane stamps a fresh app, resolves it, analyzes it and runs its tests on every push. The per-feature effect proof is assert-app-dod.mjs's `features` block; the golden matrix, the >=80% number and E2E-per-environment are all recorded cuts below

cuts.why: every intentional design change becomes N image approvals x 50 apps
a percentage of any tests is gameable; N-5 demands DISCRIMINATING tests instead — a named effect anchor and a dated mutation record

cuts.what: a manual screen-reader pass per platform
cuts.why: no Apple device; logged as a11y debt rather than carried as a gate that can never go green
downgraded to item B's human verdict; not re-mechanised here

MASTER_PLAN §4-H wins on intent, N-6 on cost: ONE web E2E is kept. The cost is stated rather than hidden — five of six platforms have no end-to-end proof under any requirement in any of the fourteen stages, and the purchase->unlock leg cannot be reversed on iOS/Android at all under store billing policy

cuts.what: the focus-not-obscured CI GATE (SC 2.4.11) — the GATE only; the criterion stays owed
cuts.by: owner 2026-08-13, on 00-COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md:445-454; NARROWED same day on the W3C research
cuts.why: PER-SCREEN. Whether the focused control is hidden behind a sticky header, a bottom sheet or a snackbar is a property of each screen's own overlay stack, so no shared-theme value can establish it and no stamp-time probe can falsify it over a chassis with two screens. Retrofit cost is ordinary, which is the half of C-14's test it fails. ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-08-13, and the narrowing is what the other four reclaims were tested against: what is cut is the CI GATE, never the CRITERION. SC 2.4.11 is LEVEL AA, so under WCAG §5.2.1 it is inside every 'Accessible — WCAG 2.2 AA' claim an app publishes; it is carried as UNMET AA DEBT in [2]C-14 beside contrast, not as an absence. Flutter does NOT give it for free — neither focus-traversal auto-scroll nor Scaffold's keyboard-inset handling stops a SnackBar, a persistent bottom sheet or a sticky header from covering a focused control, so 'the framework handles it' is not available as a reason. ~~its four siblings were cut on this same shape~~ that generalisation was wrong: the four were measured against the tree and found SATISFIED (see `reclaimed`). This entry stays a cut because nothing in the tree satisfies it and nothing in the tree can falsify it

reclaimed.title: Dragging Movements
reclaimed.by: owner 2026-08-13 — reverses the same-day cut on the W3C primary research
reclaimed.premiseThatWasFalse: 'PER-SCREEN, not chassis: … the chassis ships none [no drag gesture]' — FACTUALLY FALSE, and false about the CHASSIS itself, not merely about the frozen legacy app
reclaimed.evidence: tooling/bricks/app/__brick__/apps/{{app_id}}/lib/features/firstrun/onboarding_screen.dart:110 is a PageView.builder — a horizontal drag surface, shipped by the brick, inherited by every stamped app. Mirrored in the frozen legacy app at apps/subly/lib/features/onboarding/onboarding_screen.dart:158, whose own comment at :169 says 'PageView pans on the horizontal axis'. It CONFORMS anyway, and that is why this is a reclaim rather than a defect: SC 2.5.7 asks for a single-pointer alternative that is not path-based, and the brick ships two on the same screen — the Next FilledButton at :178-181 calls _pages.nextPage(), and the Skip TextButton at :105 calls _finish(). Legacy app equivalents: Next at :379 -> _next() -> _controller.nextPage() (:73-75), Skip at :351 -> _finish()
reclaimed.guard: the carousel must retain a non-drag advance: for every file under __brick__ that constructs a PageView, assert the same file also constructs a control whose onPressed reaches nextPage( or the finish handler. Cheap because the domain is non-empty and stays non-empty — the guard fails the day somebody deletes the button and leaves the swipe
reclaimed.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. Do not read this row as coverage
reclaimed.why: the cut priced a retrofit that does not need pricing: the alternative is already there. Leaving it cut would have published an admission of a gap the tree does not have

reclaimed.title: Consistent Help
reclaimed.state: SATISFIED (vacuously — the trigger condition is absent)
reclaimed.by: owner 2026-08-13 — reverses the same-day cut on the W3C primary research
reclaimed.premiseThatWasFalse: 'it presumes a help channel the factory does not define' — the factory does define one; what it does not do is REPEAT it, and repetition is the criterion's own trigger
reclaimed.evidence: SC 3.2.6 binds only where a help mechanism is repeated on multiple pages in a set — where it appears once, there is no relative order to be consistent about. Measured: the brick's help channel is AppConfig.supportEmail (tooling/bricks/app/__brick__/apps/{{app_id}}/lib/core/app_config.dart:40), surfaced on the Settings screen ONLY (settings_screen.dart:351 row, :500 mailto). Zero other stamped screens carry a help affordance, so the criterion's antecedent is unsatisfied and the criterion is satisfied. Legacy app matches the shape: helpAndSupport + AppConfig.contactUrl at apps/subly/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:604,606 and the mailto at :907, Settings only
reclaimed.w3cBasis: WCAG 2.2 Conformance: "if there is no content to which a success criterion applies, the success criterion is satisfied" (W3C, WCAG 2.2)
reclaimed.guard: a help affordance appearing on more than one screen must keep its relative order: count the stamped screens that reference supportEmail/contactUrl; while the count is 1 the guard prints the count and passes, and the moment it exceeds 1 it asserts the affordance sits at the same relative position in each. A count printed on every run is what stops this becoming an assertion over an empty set that nobody notices went empty
reclaimed.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. Do not read this row as coverage
reclaimed.why: LEVEL A. Cutting it while publishing 'Accessible — WCAG 2.2 AA' made the published claim false by construction under WCAG §5.2.1, and it was cut for a cost that does not exist — the criterion is already met

reclaimed.title: Redundant Entry
reclaimed.state: SATISFIED (vacuously — no process re-asks information, and the one re-entry is an explicit exception)
reclaimed.by: owner 2026-08-13 — reverses the same-day cut on the W3C primary research
reclaimed.premiseThatWasFalse: the premise ('the chassis ships no such flow') was CORRECT — the error was the conclusion drawn from it. A criterion whose trigger is absent is SATISFIED, not cut; cutting it records a gap where the standard records conformance
reclaimed.evidence: SC 3.3.7 binds only where a process asks for information already entered in the same process. Measured across the brick's auth flow: sign_up_screen.dart:142,149 (email, newPassword), sign_in_screen.dart:89,96 (email, password), reset_password_screen.dart:272,280 — no step re-asks an earlier step's answer. The single re-entry is reset-password's confirm field (:280 beside :272), which is WCAG's own named 'essential' exception to 3.3.7 (confirming a new password), and BOTH fields carry AutofillHints.newPassword so a password manager can populate them without the user retyping anything. Legacy app identical: apps/subly/lib/features/auth/sign_up_screen.dart:145,152 and reset_password_screen.dart:275,283
reclaimed.guard: no flow may re-ask information already given: within one route's widget tree, assert no two text fields declare the SAME autofillHints value unless the pair is on the register's named confirm-field allowlist (today: reset-password new/confirm). Cheap, and it fails on exactly the shape the criterion forbids
reclaimed.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. Do not read this row as coverage
reclaimed.why: LEVEL A, same §5.2.1 argument as SC 3.2.6. And the autofillHints that satisfy it already ship, so the cut priced work that was already done

reclaimed.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
reclaimed.by: owner 2026-08-13 — reverses the same-day cut on the W3C primary research
reclaimed.premiseThatWasFalse: 'The chassis ships no OTP screen … so there is nothing to assert on today' — it inverted the polarity of the criterion. PASTING an OTP is what SATISFIES 3.3.8; BLOCKING paste is what violates it. Absence of an OTP screen is therefore conformance, not an unassertable void
reclaimed.evidence: Every chassis auth field is a plain TextField whose paste path is untouched — measured, source only: enableInteractiveSelection: false -> 0 occurrences, oneTimeCode -> 0, maxLength: 1 -> 0, across tooling/bricks, apps/subly/lib and packages/*/lib. Password entry is the cognitive-function test in play, and the chassis meets 3.3.8's Mechanism exception directly: AutofillHints.password / .newPassword / .email at sign_in_screen.dart:89,96 · sign_up_screen.dart:142,149 · reset_password_screen.dart:272,280, so a password manager fills the field and nothing suppresses the paste menu
reclaimed.residualRisk: the register's original hazard was correctly identified and is KEPT as a hazard rather than as a cut: a segmented one-box-per-digit OTP field is the common way 3.3.8 is broken, and [2]C-13's auth screens are stage-5 work. That is a FUTURE RISK, not a PRESENT FAILURE, and the difference is the whole reason this row is a reclaim
reclaimed.guard: no OTP field may disable paste: assert enableInteractiveSelection: false, contextMenuBuilder returning an empty widget, and maxLength: 1 all stay at ZERO occurrences in auth-feature source. The domain is empty today and the guard must PRINT that count every run, so the day an OTP screen lands the count moves and the guard starts biting instead of silently continuing to pass
reclaimed.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. Do not read this row as coverage
reclaimed.why: cutting it recorded a failure the tree does not have, and would have carried that admission under the published AA claim. The thing worth watching is the future OTP screen, and a hazard is what this row records

claimWording.aaaAttachedAs: WCAG 2.2 §5.3.2 optional conformance-claim component — 'A list of success criteria beyond the level of conformance claimed that have been met'
claimWording.sanctionedBy: WCAG 2.2 §5.2.1 Note 1 — 'authors are encouraged to report (in their claim) any progress toward meeting success criteria from all levels beyond the achieved level of conformance'
claimWording.why: §5.2.1 is ALL-OR-NOTHING per level: a Level AAA claim requires every Level A, AA and AAA success criterion. Twenty of thirty-one is not a level, it is a list — and the standard has a place for exactly that list. Naming the route (§5.2.1 Note 1 + §5.3.2) is what stops the next person inventing 'AA+', which is not a conformance level and would be an unverifiable claim under [8]K-3

doNotUse.why: 🔴 §5.4 is for content the author does not control — third-party content injected after publication, and language-based partial conformance. It is NOT a way to say 'we met some of a higher level'. Reaching for it here would misstate a DEFINED TERM of the standard in a published legal claim, which is a worse defect than claiming nothing beyond AA at all

wcag2ictLimit.finding: WCAG2ICT covers only Level A and Level AA for non-web ICT, and explicitly DECLINES to define eight terms that AAA criteria depend on: blocks of text, context-sensitive help, motion animation, perimeter, region, section, supplemental content, user inactivity
wcag2ictLimit.consequence: For 5 of NIKATRU's 6 platforms (iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, Linux — everything except Web) there is NO NORMATIVE VEHICLE for a Level AAA conformance claim at all. Web is the only target where 'WCAG 2.2 AAA' is even a well-formed statement
wcag2ictLimit.why: this is an INDEPENDENT reason the named-set approach is correct, and it is recorded because it changes what a claim can MEAN, not merely what it costs. An agent or a store listing that later writes 'AAA' against a desktop or mobile build is asserting something the applicable interpretation document refuses to define

aaaPolicy.policy: Level AA everywhere, PLUS a named set of AAA criteria that are free or chassis-cheap. FULL AAA IS REJECTED
aaaPolicy.w3cBasis: WCAG 2.2 §5.2.1 Note 2 — 'It is not recommended that Level AAA conformance be required as a general policy for entire sites because it is not possible to satisfy all Level AAA success criteria for some content.'
aaaPolicy.countCorrection: 🔴 the brief that carried this decision said 'the 18 named AAA criteria'. Measured by enumeration 2026-08-13: 4 already-satisfied + 5 satisfied-by-absence + 10 chassis-build + 1 with-carve-out = 20. The enumeration governs. 20 + 10 + 1 = 31, which is the AAA count in WCAG 2.2, so the set is closed — that closure is the check, not the arithmetic
aaaPolicy.rungUnchanged: no row in these lists raises [2]C-14's rung. Adopted-but-unmet criteria are carried as ⬜ debt with `unmetDebt: true`, exactly as contrast and reduce-motion were on the same day

aaaAdopted.title: Target Size (Enhanced)
aaaAdopted.state: SATISFIED — the house standard is 48, the criterion asks 44
aaaAdopted.evidence: 48 logical px is enforced today at apps/subly/test/chassis_properties_test.dart:1209 and tooling/bricks/app/__brick__/apps/{{app_id}}/test/chassis_properties_test.dart:1250, both `greaterThanOrEqualTo(48.0)`. 48 > 44, so the enhanced criterion is cleared by the number already shipping. MASTER_PLAN §4-F's physical-size note is why 48 was chosen and it is unrelated to this: 44 is Apple's pt figure and WCAG's AAA CSS-px figure, and the house number clears both
aaaAdopted.⚠️ scopeLimit: 🔴 THIS IS EXACTLY AS STRONG AS THE 48px LIMB AND NO STRONGER, AND §4-F ALREADY MEASURED THAT LIMB AS COVERING LESS THAN ITS NAME. The test is titled 'every tap target on every declared route is at least 48px' but ranges over `_iconOnlyControls` (:873) — IconButton | InkWell | GestureDetector filtered to those with NO Text descendant. Every LABELLED control is outside the domain. So 2.5.5 is adopted as SATISFIED over the same partial domain, and it becomes satisfied over the WHOLE domain on the same increment that lands meetsGuideline(androidTapTargetGuideline) across the 19 swept surfaces. Adopting a criterion does not enlarge the check that was already there
aaaAdopted.costThatIsNotFree: 🔴 SC 2.5.5 HAS FEWER EXCEPTIONS THAN THE AA CRITERION IT SITS ABOVE, AND THIS REPO ALREADY RELIES ON THE MISSING ONE'S SIBLING. SC 2.5.8 (AA, new in 2.2) carries five exceptions — Spacing, Equivalent, Inline, User agent control, Essential. SC 2.5.5 (AAA, from 2.1) carries FOUR: it has NO Spacing exception. §4-F names Spacing as the exception 'dense grids and inline links depend on'. Adopting 2.5.5 therefore REMOVES Spacing from the toolbox for any surface claiming it. The 20px checkbox at apps/subly/lib/features/auth/legal_consent_fields.dart:123 survives, because it relies on EQUIVALENT (the hit area is on the label sentence — see the comment at :122-125), and Equivalent exists at both levels
aaaAdopted.guard: the existing 48px limb, WIDENED to meetsGuideline(androidTapTargetGuideline) per §4-F. No NEW guard is owed by this adoption — it is the same assertion with a lower bar than the one already asserted. What IS owed is a REFUSAL: any future exception claimed on a 2.5.5 surface must name Equivalent, Inline, User agent control or Essential, and must NOT name Spacing
aaaAdopted.guardStatus: 🟡 PARTIAL — the 48px assertion runs today over the icon-only domain; the widening to all actionable nodes is ⬜ NOT BUILT (§4-F, `meetsGuideline` measures 0 in live .dart files and assert-a11y-coverage.mjs:283-286's tap-target family has read x0 since it was written)
aaaAdopted.why: free: the number that clears it already ships and is negative-tested. The reason it is worth NAMING rather than leaving unstated is the exception delta — an adoption that quietly narrows what a future screen may justify is a cost, and an unstated cost is what this whole thread is about

aaaAdopted.title: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
aaaAdopted.state: SATISFIED
aaaAdopted.evidence: The criterion forbids RESTRICTING the input modalities available on a platform, except where the restriction is essential, required to ensure security, or required to respect user settings. Measured 2026-08-13 across packages/, apps/ and tooling/bricks (excluding build output): `PointerDeviceKind` -> 0, `supportedDevices` -> 0, `FocusNode(canRequestFocus: false)` -> 0. Nothing in the tree narrows a gesture recognizer to a device kind or removes keyboard focusability, so touch, mouse, stylus and keyboard all stay live wherever the platform offers them
aaaAdopted.guard: assert the three shapes above stay at ZERO in app and package source, and PRINT the count on every run so the day one appears the guard starts biting rather than continuing to pass. Same shape as the SC 3.3.8 paste guard, and for the same reason: the domain is empty and an empty domain that nobody prints is an assertion nobody notices went vacuous
aaaAdopted.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. Do not read this row as coverage
aaaAdopted.why: free, and free in the strongest sense: it is satisfied by NOT doing something. The realistic way it breaks is a well-meant `supportedDevices: {PointerDeviceKind.touch}` added to stop a desktop mouse triggering a swipe — which is precisely the change the printed count would catch

aaaAdopted.title: Three Flashes
aaaAdopted.state: SATISFIED
aaaAdopted.evidence: 2.3.2 forbids ANY content flashing more than three times per second (2.3.1, Level A, allows it below the general and red flash thresholds; 2.3.2 removes the threshold escape). Measured 2026-08-13: no timed-media playback exists in the tree (see `vacuityGuard` below — zero video/audio playback plugins in any pubspec.yaml), and every occurrence of the word 'flash' under tooling/bricks/app/__brick__ is about a UI interstitial appearing once at launch (router.dart:279, sign_up_screen.dart:91, onboarding_screen.dart:22, providers.dart:601 and :2183), not about repeated luminance change
aaaAdopted.guard: COVERED BY `vacuityGuard` (assert-no-timed-media.mjs) FOR ITS LARGEST RISK SURFACE, and only for that. Video is where a >3Hz flash realistically arrives; a hand-written Flutter animation that flashes faster than 3Hz is possible and NOT mechanically detectable. This is stated rather than papered over — the guard reduces the surface, it does not close the criterion
aaaAdopted.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. Do not read this row as coverage
aaaAdopted.why: free today, and it is the one adopted criterion whose residual risk is NOT mechanisable. A criterion you cannot fully guard is one you may still adopt — but you may not claim the guard closes it, which is the difference between this row and Guideline 3.1's non-adoption

aaaAdopted.title: Location
aaaAdopted.state: SATISFIED — the adaptive shell IS the location mechanism
aaaAdopted.evidence: 2.4.8 asks for information about the user's location within a set of pages. The chassis shell supplies it structurally at every window class: packages/design_system/lib/src/widgets/app_scaffold.dart declares `required this.selectedIndex` (:123, field at :136) and passes it to the bottom NavigationBar (:206-207, compact), the NavigationRail (:231-232, medium and expanded) and the permanent NavigationDrawer (large/XL). A selected destination rendered in all five classes is the location indicator, and it is inherited by every stamp rather than built per app
aaaAdopted.guard: the existing five-window-class limb of assert-stamp-properties.mjs already asserts each class renders its own navigation affordance at its exact Material edge. The ADDITION owed is one clause: the selected destination must be programmatically determinable — i.e. `selectedIndex` reaches the rendered navigation widget in every class, not merely that a navigation widget exists. Cheap, because the domain (5 classes) is already enumerated and already non-empty
aaaAdopted.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — named, not enforced. The five-class limb IS built and verified (main @ 9007e5b); the selectedIndex clause is not
aaaAdopted.why: free: the shell was built for [2]C-14's window-class limb and this criterion falls out of it. Worth naming because the mechanism is a SHARED widget — if a stamped app hand-rolls its own bar (which apps/subly does, per DoD §4-C: 'Subly hand-rolls a fixed phone bottom-bar'), it leaves the shell and this criterion stops being inherited

aaaAdopted.title: Animation from Interactions
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET — MEASURED UNBUILT
aaaAdopted.evidence: already adopted into [2]C-14 on 2026-08-13 as the reduce-motion limb, and already measured unbuilt on the same day: disableAnimations -> 0 files, reduceMotion -> 0, AnimationsDisabled -> 0, prefers-reduced-motion -> 0, across packages/ apps/ tooling/bricks/ (source only). The reduce-motion API surface is ABSENT ENTIRELY, not merely unasserted

Its debt is unchanged and [2]C-14's rung is unchanged

aaaAdopted.title: Re-authenticating
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET
aaaAdopted.evidence: the session model exists — packages/core/lib/src/auth/auth_models.dart:103,111,123 carries `expiresAt` and an expiry test, and auth_event.dart:84-103 classifies expiredOrUsed. What does NOT exist is the criterion's actual requirement: that after re-authenticating, the user can CONTINUE THE ACTIVITY WITHOUT LOSS OF DATA. No draft-preservation-across-reauth path was found
aaaAdopted.guard: on a fresh stamp, a form with unsaved input that hits a session expiry must restore that input after re-authentication. Testable at stamp time because the chassis owns both halves — the auth seam ([2]C-15) and the form screens
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap ONCE: it is one interception point in the shared auth seam plus one draft-holding convention, and it is near-impossible to retrofit into 50 apps' forms individually. Directly coupled to DoD §4-A's account-deletion+reauth screen, which already forces a reauth path to exist

aaaAdopted.title: Timeouts
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET
aaaAdopted.evidence: 2.2.6 requires that users are WARNED of the duration of any user inactivity that could cause data loss, unless the data is preserved for more than 20 hours of inactivity. No inactivity warning and no such preservation guarantee was found in the chassis
aaaAdopted.guard: either the chassis preserves user data across >20h of inactivity (in which case the criterion is met by the storage policy and the guard asserts the policy), or the shared session layer emits a warning naming the duration. One or the other, asserted at the seam — not per screen
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap because it is a property of ONE session layer, and it pairs with 2.2.5: the same interception point that preserves a draft across reauth is the one that knows the inactivity budget. ⚠️ WCAG2ICT explicitly DECLINES to define 'user inactivity' for non-web ICT — so on 5 of 6 platforms this criterion is adopted as a HOUSE requirement whose term has no normative non-web definition. Named, not hidden

aaaAdopted.title: Error Prevention (All)
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET
aaaAdopted.evidence: 3.3.4 (AA) requires reversible/checked/confirmed submission for legal, financial and data-modifying pages; 3.3.6 (AAA) extends the SAME requirement to ALL pages requiring the user to submit information. DoD §4-B already demands `confirming(destructive->reauth)` on async actions, which is the mechanism — what is missing is that it applies to EVERY submitting form, not only destructive ones
aaaAdopted.guard: every route in the stamped screen register that submits information must offer at least one of: reversal, error-checking with correction opportunity, or a confirm step. The screen register from [2]C-13 / assert-screen-set.mjs already enumerates the 22 screens, so the domain exists and is non-empty — this is a clause on an existing enumeration, not a new sweep
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap because DoD §4-B's form state machine (pristine/editing/inline-error/submitting/server-error/success/offline-queued) already contains the error-checking limb; 3.3.6 is that machine applied without the 'only if legal/financial' filter. Retrofitting it across 50 apps' forms is the expensive direction

aaaAdopted.title: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET — but MUCH closer than the others, and the measurement says so
aaaAdopted.evidence: 3.3.9 removes 3.3.8's Object Recognition and Personal Content exceptions: NO cognitive function test at all, unless an alternative or a Mechanism is provided. The chassis already satisfies 3.3.8 via the Mechanism exception, and that SAME mechanism carries 3.3.9 — 3.3.9 keeps the Alternative and Mechanism exceptions and drops only the other two. Measured (reclaimed row `accessible-auth-paste-otp`, 2026-08-13): AutofillHints.password/.newPassword/.email at sign_in_screen.dart:89,96, sign_up_screen.dart:142,149, reset_password_screen.dart:272,280; enableInteractiveSelection: false -> 0, oneTimeCode -> 0, maxLength: 1 -> 0
aaaAdopted.guard: the SC 3.3.8 guard named in `reclaimed`, PLUS one clause 3.3.8 does not need: no auth step may require the user to recognise an OBJECT or personal content (the two exceptions 3.3.9 removes) — i.e. no image-selection or picture-password challenge in an auth route. Zero today, and the count prints every run
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap because the AA sibling is already satisfied by a mechanism that also satisfies the AAA one. The delta is a REFUSAL — never add an image-recognition challenge — which costs nothing to hold and is expensive to undo once a CAPTCHA-style gate is in 50 apps

aaaAdopted.title: Focus Appearance
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET — MEASURED UNBUILT
aaaAdopted.evidence: 2.4.13 requires the focus indicator to have an area at least the size of a 2px-thick perimeter of the unfocused component AND a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 between focused and unfocused states. Measured 2026-08-13 across packages/design_system/lib and tooling/bricks/app/__brick__: focusColor -> 0, focusedBorder -> 0, WidgetState.focused -> 0, MaterialState.focused -> 0. NOTHING in the shared theme specifies a focus indicator; every stamped app inherits Material's default, which the theme has never asserted anything about
aaaAdopted.guard: the shared theme must specify a focus indicator, and a stamp-time probe must assert its thickness and its focused/unfocused contrast ratio. Naturally paired with the 1.4.6 contrast limb, because both are computations over the SAME shared ColorScheme and the tree computes no ratio today (contrastRatio -> 0 files, computeLuminance -> 0 files)
aaaAdopted.why: the canonical C-14 shape: one theme value, inherited by 50 apps, near-impossible to retrofit once shipped. ⚠️ WCAG2ICT declines to define 'perimeter' for non-web ICT, so on 5 of 6 platforms the SIZE limb has no normative non-web reading and the house adopts the CSS-px reading by choice. The contrast limb is unaffected

aaaAdopted.title: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET
aaaAdopted.🔴 supersedes: SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), Level AA — STRICTLY. 2.4.11 forbids the focused component being ENTIRELY hidden; 2.4.12 forbids ANY PART of it being hidden. 2.4.12 met implies 2.4.11 met, always
aaaAdopted.consequenceForTheCutList: 🔴 STATED BECAUSE TWO ROWS OF THIS REGISTER WOULD OTHERWISE CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. `cuts` -> `focus-not-obscured` cuts the CI GATE for SC 2.4.11 on the reasoning that 'no shared-theme value can establish it and no stamp-time probe can falsify it over a chassis with two screens'. Adopting the STRICTLY STRONGER 2.4.12 as a chassis build asserts that a probe CAN be written. Both cannot stand unexamined. The resolution recorded here, and it is a SEQUENCING one, not a reversal: the 2.4.11 GATE CUT STANDS TODAY and is not touched by this adoption — but the increment that builds 2.4.12's probe discharges 2.4.11's AA debt by the same work, and ON THAT DAY the 2.4.11 gate cut must be re-opened with the owner rather than left standing as an admission of a gap the code no longer has. That is the same defect as the 2026-08-13 over-cut, arriving on a timer
aaaAdopted.guard: a stamp-time probe that focuses each interactive node on each declared route and asserts no author-created content intersects its semantics rect — with the overlay stack (SnackBar, persistent bottom sheet, sticky header) deliberately populated, since an empty overlay stack makes the assertion vacuous. THIS IS THE LIMB THE 2.4.11 CUT SAID COULD NOT BE WRITTEN; adopting 2.4.12 is a commitment to write it
aaaAdopted.why: Flutter gives NEITHER criterion for free — neither focus-traversal auto-scroll nor Scaffold's keyboard-inset handling stops a SnackBar or a sticky header covering a focused control (recorded in the `focus-not-obscured` cut). Adopted here because the overlay stack is CHASSIS-OWNED: the shared shell decides where snackbars and sheets appear, so one policy in one place covers 50 apps

aaaAdopted.title: Keyboard (No Exception)
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET (unmeasured — no keyboard-operability sweep exists)
aaaAdopted.evidence: 2.1.1 (A) allows an exception for functionality requiring path-dependent input; 2.1.3 removes it. The chassis's one path-dependent surface is the onboarding PageView.builder (__brick__/…/features/firstrun/onboarding_screen.dart:110) — and it already ships Next (:178) and Skip (:105), which is why SC 2.5.7 was reclaimed as SATISFIED. The same two controls are what 2.1.3 needs, PROVIDED they are keyboard-reachable. That has never been asserted: no keyboard-traversal test exists in the chassis suite
aaaAdopted.guard: on a fresh stamp, every declared route must be fully operable by keyboard alone — traverse with Tab/Shift-Tab and Enter/Space and assert every actionable node is reachable and activatable. Non-empty domain by construction (the 22-screen register), so it cannot go vacuous
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap because Flutter gives most of it for free and the ONE path-dependent surface is a brick screen, not an app screen. The cost of adoption is a standing refusal: no stamped app may add a drag-only, swipe-only or gesture-only path without a keyboard equivalent — cheap to hold, expensive to retrofit across 50 apps

aaaAdopted.title: Change on Request
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET
aaaAdopted.evidence: 3.2.5 requires that changes of context are initiated only by user request, or that a mechanism exists to turn them off. The chassis ships several AUTOMATIC context changes by design: the router's consent/terms interstitial (core/router.dart:279), the re-accept-terms redirect (features/auth/reaccept_terms_screen.dart), and the force-update wall. Each is an author-initiated context change the user did not request
aaaAdopted.guard: enumerate every automatic redirect in the shared router and require each to be on a named allowlist carrying its 3.2.5 justification — the criterion's own exceptions are narrow, and a legal-consent gate or a force-update wall is defensible where a silent navigation is not. The router is chassis-owned and the redirect set is small and enumerable, which is what makes this cheap
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap because ALL of these live in ONE shared router; the same requirement applied per app would mean auditing 50 routers. ⚠️ Honest cost: the force-update wall and the consent interstitial are non-negotiable product requirements (DoD §4-A), so adopting 3.2.5 means committing to justify them under its exceptions rather than to remove them — and if that justification does not hold, this row becomes the first adopted criterion the factory cannot meet

aaaAdopted.title: Images of Text (No Exception)
aaaAdopted.state: SATISFIED TODAY, adopted as a standing refusal
aaaAdopted.evidence: 1.4.9 permits images of text ONLY where the presentation is essential or the image is customizable. Measured 2026-08-13 — every image asset in the tree: apps/subly/assets/brand/{nikatru-icon.png, nikatru-logo.png, nikatru-logo-dark-bg.png} and apps/subly/assets/icon/{app_icon_1024.png, app_icon_background.png/.svg, app_icon_foreground.png/.svg, app_icon_maskable.svg}. Every one is a LOGOTYPE or a launcher icon. WCAG names logotypes under Essential: 'text that is part of a logo or brand name' is the standard's own worked example of essential presentation. So the criterion is met, and it is met by the exception rather than by absence
aaaAdopted.guard: 🔴 THE OBVIOUS GUARD IS THE WRONG ONE. 'No image asset may contain text' fails on the brand logo — an assertion that fires on conforming content, which is worse than none because it gets disabled. The correct shape: every image asset declared in a pubspec `assets:` block must be on a register naming its 1.4.9 disposition — `logotype` (Essential, the four brand/icon files today) or `no-text`. A new asset with no disposition fails the build. This reuses the same pattern as tooling/legal/asset-register.json rather than inventing a second register
aaaAdopted.why: chassis-cheap as a REFUSAL held from day one: text baked into a bitmap cannot be localized ([2] DoD §4-E, zero hardcoded strings) and cannot be text-scaled (the TextScaler.clamp limb), so 1.4.9 is already implied by two invariants the chassis enforces. It is worth naming because the pressure to bake text into an image is real — store screenshots and onboarding art — and 50 apps' worth of it is unretrofittable

aaaAdopted.title: Contrast (Enhanced)
aaaAdopted.state: ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET
aaaAdopted.carveOut: TEXT ONLY. Non-text contrast stays at SC 1.4.11's Level AA 3:1
aaaAdopted.🔴 carveOutIsAlreadyTheStandard: MEASURED CORRECTION, 2026-08-13. SC 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced) IS ALREADY TEXT-ONLY IN THE STANDARD — it reads 'text and images of text', with exceptions for large text (4.5:1), incidental text, and logotypes. WCAG 2.2 has NO AAA non-text contrast criterion at all; 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA, 3:1) is the only one at any level. So the carve-out as written removes nothing from the criterion. What it actually constrains is the IMPLEMENTATION: it forbids buying 1.4.6 by raising Flutter's scheme-wide `contrastLevel`, because that knob moves text and non-text roles TOGETHER. Recorded this way because 'we carved non-text out of 1.4.6' would misstate the standard, while 'we refuse the scheme-wide knob' is the decision actually being made
aaaAdopted.evidence: 🔬 MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-13 with material_color_utilities 0.13.0 (the package Flutter's ColorScheme.fromSeed is built on), SchemeTonalSpot — fromSeed's default variant — light brightness, six far-apart brand seeds (red #D32F2F, orange #F57C00, green #388E3C, teal #00796B, blue #1976D2, purple #7B1FA2). AT contrastLevel 0.0, WHICH IS WHAT SHIPS: primary/onPrimary 6.42-6.46 · secondary/onSecondary 6.45-6.49 · surfaceVariant/onSurfaceVariant 7.21-7.26 · surface/onSurface 16.27-16.36 · outline/surface 4.27-4.28. So the SEEDED chassis path ALREADY clears 4.5:1 (the adopted AA limb) on every pair measured, ALREADY clears 1.4.6's 7:1 on surface/onSurface and surfaceVariant/onSurfaceVariant, and MISSES 7:1 on exactly two pairs — primary/onPrimary and secondary/onSecondary — by about 0.55 of a ratio point. That is the operative 1.4.6 gap, and it is much narrower than 'unmeasured'
aaaAdopted.🔴 whyNotContrastLevel: 🔬 MEASURED, SAME RUN. contrastLevel 1.0: every pair clears 7:1 (primary/onPrimary 13.91-14.02, secondary/onSecondary 13.92-14.02, surfaceVariant/onSurfaceVariant 16.24-16.31, outline/surface 13.23-13.36) — and primary collapses to TONE 17.9-18.1, i.e. near-black, where hue is far harder to perceive. contrastLevel 0.5 also clears 7:1 everywhere (primary/onPrimary 12.01-12.09, outline/surface 7.37-7.45) at tone 22.6-22.8. THE BRIEF'S FIGURE IS LOCATED: '13.25-13.33:1' is the OUTLINE/SURFACE pair at contrastLevel 1.0 — measured here as 13.23-13.36 — which is a NON-TEXT pair, 1.4.11's subject, not 1.4.6's. And a sharper correction: 'flattens all brands to near-identical lightness' is TRUE AT EVERY CONTRAST LEVEL INCLUDING THE ONE WE SHIP — tonalSpot pins primary to tone 40.0-40.2 across those same six seeds at contrastLevel 0.0. Brands are differentiated by HUE (23/53/146/183/259/320 degrees), never by lightness. The real cost of raising the knob is therefore NOT lost lightness variance (there was none) but moving primary from tone 40, where hue reads, to tone 18-23, where it does not. Same conclusion, correct mechanism
aaaAdopted.whyItMattersForC11: [2]C-11 exists because a `primary: AppColors.accent` override made every seeded theme paint identically and nothing caught it for months. Store-clone detection depends on 50 apps looking DIFFERENT. A scheme-wide contrastLevel raise is the same failure with a virtuous motive: it would clear every pair and re-flatten the portfolio, and C-11's guard would be the only thing standing between it and 50 identical-looking apps
aaaAdopted.guard: compute the ACTUAL ratio for every foreground/background pair the shared theme puts on screen, and assert >=7:1 for normal text, >=4.5:1 for large text, with named exceptions for incidental text and logotypes; non-text pairs assert >=3:1 under 1.4.11 and are NOT raised. Nothing in the tree computes a ratio today (contrastRatio -> 0 files, computeLuminance -> 0 files), so the first increment is the computation itself
aaaAdopted.residualRisk: 🔴 THE MEASUREMENT ABOVE COVERS THE SEEDED PATH ONLY, AND THE RISKY PATH IS THE OTHER ONE. buildAppTheme(seed:) calls ColorScheme.fromSeed with no role override, so its pairs are contrast-correct by construction — that is what was measured. The pinned legacy path in the same file, AppTheme.light()/AppTheme.dark(), pins primary/secondary/surface to hand-picked AppColors constants WHILE letting onPrimary/onSurface stay generated from the seed's palette. That is the shape that silently breaks a pair, it is UNMEASURED, and it is the path apps/subly runs on (MASTER_PLAN §4-D)
aaaAdopted.why: adopted because contrast lives in ONE shared theme and retrofitting it means re-deriving every shipped app's palette and re-shooting every store screenshot on six platforms. The carve-out is what keeps the adoption compatible with [2]C-11's store-clone-detection purpose

vacuityGuard.guardStatus: ⬜ NOT BUILT — SPECIFIED HERE, NOT ENFORCED ANYWHERE
vacuityGuard.whyItExists: Five adopted criteria are satisfied ONLY because no app plays video or audio. W3C: 'if there is no content to which a success criterion applies, the success criterion is satisfied.' A VACUOUS CLAIM WITH NO GUARD GOES FALSE SILENTLY — the day someone adds an onboarding video, five published conformance statements become untrue and nothing anywhere goes red. This is the same shape as the four criteria reclaimed earlier on 2026-08-13, with one difference that decides the guard: those four range over domains that are non-empty and STAY non-empty, whereas these five are true about an ABSENCE, and an absence is what a single commit reverses
vacuityGuard.🔴 theBriefsScopeWasMeasuredWRONG: The decision arrived asking for a guard that 'fails if any video/audio asset enters an APP BUNDLE'. Measured 2026-08-13, that guard would have been GREEN ON A REPO THAT ALREADY CONTAINS A MANIFEST-DECLARED MP3, and would have stayed green through the exact change it was written to catch. THE MEASUREMENTS: (1) tooling/content_pipeline/src/formats.mjs FORMAT_ALLOWLIST ALREADY CARRIES `{format:'mp3', modality:'audio'}`, locked by [ADR 017] — audio is a DELIBERATELY ALLOWED pack format, not an oversight. (2) packages/core/test/fixtures/pack/v1/assets/tone/confirm.mp3 exists and is DECLARED in that pack's manifest.json assets list with its sha256; assert-pack-inert.mjs:145-159 runs live negative tests against those very bytes. (3) [ADR 019] locks audio/TTS to Google Cloud Chirp 3 HD and banks it as content — so the pack rail is the DESIGNED delivery route for audio, and it is not an app-bundle asset at all. A bundle-scoped guard watches the door nobody is going to use

limbs.name: BUNDLED ASSETS
limbs.what: walk every pubspec.yaml under apps/, packages/ and tooling/bricks/**/__brick__/**, parse the `flutter: assets:` list, resolve each entry (a trailing-slash entry ships the whole directory, so walk it), and refuse any file whose BYTES are a timed-media container
limbs.bytesNotExtensions: the repo's own rule, from assert-pack-inert.mjs:13 — 'a .mp3 holding WebP bytes and a .webp holding MP3 bytes are the same defect, a file lying about itself'. Reuse tooling/content_pipeline/src/formats.mjs's matcher shapes rather than writing a second set of magic bytes; two allowlists is how they drift
limbs.measuredToday: the only `assets:` block in the tree is apps/subly/pubspec.yaml:181-182 -> assets/brand/, holding three PNGs. Zero timed media. PRINT that count

limbs.name: THE PACK FORMAT ALLOWLIST
limbs.what: assert FORMAT_ALLOWLIST carries no entry with modality 'video', and — because it DOES carry one with modality 'audio' — assert that the audio entry stays paired with limb 3's absent player, printing both facts every run
limbs.halfOfThisALREADYEXISTS: assert-pack-inert.mjs:72 already fails the build if the allowlist gains a video modality ('Video is DORMANT — 39-CHASSIS §4 cut 8'). THE VIDEO HALF IS BUILT AND WIRED (ci.yml:1801). The AUDIO half is not built and CANNOT take the same shape, because audio is deliberately allowed by [ADR 017] — which is precisely why limb 3 is the load-bearing one

limbs.name: THE PLAYER
limbs.what: no pubspec.yaml anywhere in the repo may depend on a timed-media playback plugin — video_player, chewie, media_kit, just_audio, audioplayers, audio_session or equivalents. Measured 2026-08-13: ZERO across every pubspec.yaml in the tree. PRINT the count
limbs.🔴 whyThisIsTheLOADBEARINGLIMB: a pack MP3 with no player is inert bytes; a PLAYER is what turns bytes into 'audio content' in WCAG's sense, and therefore what makes 1.2.6-1.2.9 and 1.4.7 bind. It is also the ONLY limb that can cover SC 1.2.9 Audio-only (Live), whose content arrives over the network with no asset to inspect. A guard without this limb inspects files while the criterion turns on capability

vacuityGuard.printEveryRun: 🔴 ALL THREE LIMBS MUST PRINT THEIR COUNTS ON EVERY RUN, PASSING OR FAILING. Every limb quantifies over a domain that is empty or near-empty today, and this repo's recorded failure mode is not a broken check but a check that silently stopped checking. A printed zero is a zero somebody can see move; an unprinted one is indistinguishable from a scanner that stopped scanning
negativeTestsRequiredBeforeTrustingIt: drop a real MP3 into apps/subly/assets/brand/ and add it to the pubspec assets list -> limb 1 must fail, naming the file and the bytes
add {format:'webm', modality:'video'} to FORMAT_ALLOWLIST -> limb 2 must fail (this one is already provable today against assert-pack-inert.mjs:72)
add `video_player: ^2.0.0` to any pubspec.yaml -> limb 3 must fail, naming the pubspec
rename a WebP to .mp4 and declare it -> limb 1 must NOT fail (bytes govern, and a guard that fires on conforming content gets disabled)

🔴 AND THE ONE THAT PROVES THE SCOPE FIX: run the guard AS THE BRIEF ORIGINALLY SCOPED IT (limb 1 alone) against the tree as it stands -> it must pass, while packages/core/test/fixtures/pack/v1/assets/tone/confirm.mp3 sits declared in a manifest. That green run IS the finding, and it is the reason limbs 2 and 3 exist
vacuityGuard.conditionalityMustBeRecordedOnTheClaim: the five criteria are adopted as CONDITIONAL: each row carries `conditionalOn: vacuityGuard`, and until the guard is built each is a vacuous claim with no tripwire. Attaching them to a published §5.3.2 optional component BEFORE the guard exists would put five statements under [8]K-3 that nothing can falsify

aaaNotAdopted.title: Unusual Words
aaaNotAdopted.why: GUIDELINE 3.1 READABLE IS NOT ADOPTED IN FULL — all four of its AAA criteria are refused for one reason. Every one is a property of CONTENT, per app, times 50 apps, times every locale the app ships. And no CI guard is possible: whether a word is 'used in an unusual or restricted way' is a judgement about meaning in context, which no parser reaches. 📌 A CRITERION YOU CANNOT GUARD IS ONE YOU SHOULD NOT CLAIM — it decays silently on the next copy edit, and a silently-decaying claim under [8]K-3 is worse than an honest non-adoption

aaaNotAdopted.title: Abbreviations
aaaNotAdopted.why: same Guideline 3.1 reasoning: per app x 50 x every locale, and unguardable. Detecting an abbreviation mechanically is possible; knowing whether its expanded form is available on FIRST use in that locale's copy is not

aaaNotAdopted.title: Reading Level
aaaNotAdopted.why: same Guideline 3.1 reasoning, PLUS a specific blocker worth recording on its own: 3.1.5 asks for text at a lower-secondary reading level, and THERE IS NO ACCEPTED LOWER-SECONDARY READABILITY MEASURE FOR TAMIL. The criterion cannot be evaluated, let alone guarded, in a locale the factory ships. Adopting it would mean publishing a claim about text nobody can measure

aaaNotAdopted.title: Pronunciation
aaaNotAdopted.why: same Guideline 3.1 reasoning. Whether pronunciation is 'essential to the meaning' of a specific word in specific copy is a per-string editorial judgement in every locale

aaaNotAdopted.title: Visual Presentation
aaaNotAdopted.why: it requires the user to be able to SELECT foreground and background colours, set line spacing to at least 1.5, set paragraph spacing to at least 1.5x line spacing, and resize to 200% without horizontal scrolling — i.e. it ships a USER THEME EDITOR. That fights brand differentiation head-on: [2]C-11 exists so 50 apps look distinguishable for store-clone detection, and a user-repaintable theme makes the brand a suggestion. The 200% resize limb is already met by the TextScaler.clamp(1.0, 2.0) limb; the colour-selection limb is the one refused

aaaNotAdopted.title: Help
aaaNotAdopted.why: context-sensitive help for every form control is a CONTENT half, per app. The chassis can ship the affordance; it cannot write 50 apps' help text. ⚠️ Note the difference from SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help (Level A), which IS satisfied and is in `reclaimed`: 3.2.6 is about the ORDER of a help mechanism that exists, 3.3.5 is about help CONTENT existing at all. Also: WCAG2ICT explicitly declines to define 'context-sensitive help' for non-web ICT

aaaNotAdopted.title: Link Purpose (Link Only)
aaaNotAdopted.why: it requires every link's purpose to be identifiable from its LINK TEXT ALONE, without surrounding context — which is a property of each app's own copy, per app x 50. The AA sibling 2.4.4 (Link Purpose in Context) is inside the AA claim and is unaffected

aaaNotAdopted.title: Section Headings
aaaNotAdopted.why: headings organise each app's own content, which is the per-app half by definition. ⚠️ WCAG2ICT also declines to define 'section' for non-web ICT, so on 5 of 6 platforms the criterion has no normative reading even if it were adopted

aaaNotAdopted.title: Identify Purpose
aaaNotAdopted.why: MARKUP-SCOPED AND UNDEFINED FOR NATIVE. 1.3.6 asks that the purpose of UI components, icons and regions be programmatically determinable — and its sufficient techniques are ARIA/microdata vocabularies with no native equivalent. WCAG2ICT declines to define 'region' for non-web ICT. So this is not a cost decision at all: on 5 of 6 platforms the criterion has no well-formed meaning to adopt

aaaNotAdopted.title: No Timing
aaaNotAdopted.why: 🔴 IT FORECLOSES WHOLE PRODUCT CATEGORIES. 2.2.3 permits timing ONLY where it is essential to real-time events or non-interactive media — which rules out timers, quizzes, games and drills. A 50-app factory wants those categories. This is the ONE non-adoption on this list driven by PRODUCT SCOPE rather than cost or measurability, and stating that plainly is the point: it is a deliberate refusal to constrain the portfolio, not an admission of an unbuilt thing. ⚠️ Note it does NOT weaken the AA claim: SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (Level A) stays inside the AA claim, so any timer a future app ships must still be adjustable, extendable or turn-off-able

aaaAwaitingOwner.title: Interruptions
aaaAwaitingOwner.state: ⬜ UNCLASSIFIED — NOT NAMED BY THE 2026-08-13 BRIEF, IN EITHER LIST
aaaAwaitingOwner.surfacedBy: an agent closing the AAA set 2026-08-13; NOT an owner decision
aaaAwaitingOwner.🔴 whyItIsParkedRatherThanSorted: WCAG 2.2 has 31 AAA success criteria. The brief named 20 to adopt and 10 to refuse. 20 + 10 = 30. SC 2.2.4 Interruptions is the thirty-first and appears in NEITHER list — which is EXACTLY the defect this entire §4-F thread was opened to fix ('a criterion in neither list is the bug'), reproduced inside the fix. Filing it into a list the owner never chose would repeat the 2026-08-13 over-cut in the same direction: a classification nobody made, read later as one somebody did. So it is recorded, measured and left for the owner
aaaAwaitingOwner.measured: the domain is NOT empty — the chassis ships several author-initiated interruptions today: packages/notifications/lib/src/local_notification_service.dart, packages/platform_storage/lib/src/in_app_review_prompter.dart + packages/core/lib/src/review/review_prompter.dart (the in-app-review prompt DoD §4-A requires), the force-update wall (referenced in __brick__/…/lib/state/providers.dart and core/app_config.dart), and dialogs/snackbars/banners across 6 brick screens (settings_screen.dart alone has 8)
aaaAwaitingOwner.theQuestion: 2.2.4 requires that interruptions can be POSTPONED OR SUPPRESSED by the user, except for emergencies. Push notifications arguably inherit the platform's own notification settings as that mechanism (a User Agent control). The force-update wall and the in-app-review prompt do NOT: neither can be postponed or suppressed by the user today. So a straight adoption would land as ⬜ ADOPTED AND UNMET with a real build behind it, and a straight refusal would be the first non-adoption on this list with no cost or measurability reason behind it
aaaAwaitingOwner.recommendation: ADOPT with the review-prompt half as chassis-cheap debt (a 'don't ask again' affordance is one shared control) and record the force-update wall under 2.2.4's emergency/essential reading, exactly as SC 3.2.5's row proposes to justify the same wall. But this is a RECOMMENDATION, not a decision — the row stays in this list until the owner moves it
